pages.text: The canal was very quiet that morning. Pongi came out carrying a bucket.
"Today I'm going to catch the biggest one." Pongi peered into the water.
Little fish swam past her feet, one after another. Pongi let them all go.
A big shadow came toward them. "I'll catch it for you," said Dad.
Dad gave his suspenders a tug. He took a deep breath.
Splash! Dad stretched both arms right out.
Slip! The fish slid between Dad's arms. The fish was gone, and only Dad was left sitting in the water.
Pongi's bucket was empty. Only water sloshed inside.
Pongi's little brother came over with a bucket. It was full of little fish.
Pongi's little brother put the bucket in front of Pongi, then gripped the shell tightly again.
